brief: This TME long-weekend digest strings together five desk calls. ABN Amro: EU gas storage sits at 65% against an 82% five-year average and a 90% target, with Qatari LNG exports down roughly 96% after Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Below about 30% storage, withdrawal capacity degrades, so a cold snap toward that level could reprice TTF toward €100-150+/MWh as scarcity turns physical, a tail EUR and STOXX vol have not priced. DB's Henry Allen: rates markets underprice coming inflation pressure, so either inflation rolls over or rates rise and risk assets adjust. JPM: US real policy rates are near 2% and the dollar's yield share is at a 25-year high of 50%, projected to reach 58% on three more hikes, though JPM views the dollar as 3-4% cheap and calls shorting it an imperfect debasement trade. BofA: prefers a VIX calendar call-spread collar (sell the Oct 16 put, buy the Nov 22-30 call spread) because SPX prices only a 0.82% post-election move, flags a copper squeeze from tariff front-running plus AI grid capex, and notes a tech-fund outflow since June. GS: cheap Korea valuations and record EWZ call open interest amid a Brazil short squeeze.
